findings.title: WITHDRAWN AS A FALSE GREEN, caught by an audit of my own instrument rather than by a re-walk.
findings.detail: WITHDRAWN AS A FALSE GREEN, caught by an audit of my own instrument rather than by a re-walk. This row was banked declared-na on the explicit claim that the project detail offers 'ZERO commit-shaped controls'. That claim was wrong: my commit detector's verb list was entirely ADDITIVE (save, send, add, submit, publish, generate...) and recognised no DESTRUCTIVE verb, so it could not see a Delete. With the list extended to delete, remove, discard, clear, archive, revoke, cancel, unpublish and reset, the same scoped enumeration of #detail-view immediately reported a Delete control. The view therefore DOES commit, and destructively - which makes it one of the more consequential views on this page, not one of the emptier ones. It needs a real walk: does the delete confirm before destroying, does a second press destroy twice, does the surface say what was removed and whether it can be undone, and - specific to this page - what happens to a project's items, links, roles, progress logs and change orders when the project they hang off is deleted. That last question is already this page's CD invariant ('deleting or archiving a project leaves no orphan item, link, role, progress log or change order') and it is exactly the kind of thing a false declared-na would have hidden. The same audit found the identical gap had made engineering-design's History pane look inputless while it carried five Delete buttons, and that a destructive control is precisely where a double-tap costs something - so the omission was worst where it mattered most.

observed.cause: commit-verb list had no destructive verbs
observed.needs: a real walk of the delete, incl. the orphan-cascade invariant

evidence.asserts: a second press on Delete cannot hide two projects
evidence.checked: LIVE WALK with every projects write held and counted. Pressed Delete TWICE: zero writes - the confirm gate absorbs both. Confirming once then fired exactly one PATCH. MEASURED WITH EVERY projects PATCH HELD, so the gate was tested without hiding a real project: pressing Delete opened the confirm and fired ZERO writes; pressing it again still ZERO; Cancel still ZERO; press-then-confirm fired exactly ONE. The stacked-dialog wart seen here (a second press opens a second confirm), recorded rather than glossed: nothing is written and no state changes, but a double-tapper dismisses twice. It is a dialog-layer fix, not this row's defect. ★THE MECHANISM IS A SOFT DELETE, AND THE CONFIRMATION USED TO DENY IT. deleteProject() is an UPDATE stamping deleted_at - not a DELETE - and three separate loaders filter with .is('deleted_at', null), so the row survives and is simply hidden. Its confirm dialog is admirably precise about this ('Soft-delete project WO-2026-001? It will be hidden from views.'), and then the success toast collapsed it into 'Deleted.' - a word that means the opposite. It now reads 'Deleted -> hidden from your project views. The record is kept, so this can be reversed.', verified off the live surface. THE SAME WORD SAT ON THE OPPOSITE TRUTH ELSEWHERE: engineering-design's Delete is a genuine hard delete with no restore path, and also said 'Deleted.'. One sentence cannot be right in both places, so each now states its own mechanism - reversible here, permanent there. AND IT SETTLES THIS PAGE'S ORPHAN QUESTION FAVOURABLY: because the project row persists, its items, links, roles, progress logs and change orders still reference a row that EXISTS, so soft-deletion cannot orphan them. That is the CD invariant's easy half; the hard half - what happens on a real purge - is not touched by this path and remains that row's business. THIS ROW WAS WITHDRAWN AS A FALSE GREEN EARLIER IN THIS SAME SESSION AND IS NOW EARNED. It had been banked declared-na on the claim that the project detail offers 'ZERO commit-shaped controls' - untrue, because my commit detector's verb list was entirely ADDITIVE and could not see a Delete. With destructive verbs recognised the same scoped enumeration found it immediately, the three rows were withdrawn, and this is the walk that replaces the guess. ★AND THE STACKED-DIALOG WART IS NOW FIXED, in the shared builder rather than on this page. Both destructive controls audited this session (this one and its counterpart on the other page) stacked a SECOND confirm dialog on a second press, and cancelling dismissed only the top one - leaving an identical question waiting behind it. Nothing was ever written, which is why these rows passed on their own terms, but on a destructive control an extra dialog is exactly where a person clicks through on autopilot. Because both cases came from ONE builder (utils.js _mount, behind whConfirm/whPrompt), the fix belongs there: while a confirm is open a second request now resolves FALSE - the safe answer, since false can only decline an action, never perform one - instead of opening a rival dialog. The gate is released in dispose() FIRST and unconditionally, because a guard that fails to release would be worse than the wart it replaces: every later confirm on the page would silently resolve false and destructive controls would appear dead. RE-MEASURED ON BOTH PAGES: a second press now yields ONE dialog (was two), Cancel leaves ZERO (was one stranded), and press-then-confirm still fires exactly one write - so the gate releases.

value_checked.wart: FIXED in utils.js _mount: one confirm at a time; second request resolves false
